02 — Material Palette

The material language, top to bottom

One consistent system runs through every room in this package: dark, matte concrete-look surfaces for grounding/wet areas, light natural wood for warmth, and matte black hardware to unify the two. No warm gold, no glossy finishes, no busy patterns — the contrast between dark and light material does the design work.

Dark Concrete
Charcoal microcement or large-format matte porcelain tile mimicking poured concrete. Used on: shower walls/floor, accent walls, select vanity counters.
Light Wood
Light oak or ash — natural, low-sheen finish with visible horizontal grain. Used on: vanity cabinetry, flooring, closet built-ins, select accent walls.
Hardware
Matte black throughout — faucets, shower valves, door hardware, light fixtures. This is the unifying thread between wood and concrete.
Walls (Living)
Warm off-white / soft neutral matte paint — not stark white. Lets wood and concrete carry the contrast.
Lighting
Recessed can lights (per plan) + warm-toned (2700K–3000K) accent sconces at vanity. Avoid cool/blue-white bulbs — kills the wood warmth.
Avoid
Glossy tile, brushed brass/gold hardware, high-contrast patterned floors, cool-gray undertones in the wood selection.
